artifacts.synopsis: TE Aaron Myers appealed Illiana Presbytery's decision to elevate his censures from indefinite suspension from office and from the Sacraments to excommunication and deposition, without any additional judicial process. The SJC sustained the appeal 21-1, holding that due process principles require some form of process before censure may be elevated, though the majority held that full de novo judicial process was not required; the sole dissent (RE Eggert) argued that Traditional Process under the BCO Rules of Discipline was required, and a concurring opinion (Sartorius) also argued for full BCO process.

artifacts.title: Adams v. Northeast Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: TE Philip J. Adams complained about a Northeast Presbytery judicial matter while a related appeal was pending and sought a retrial of charges on which the accused had been acquitted. The SJC ruled the complaint administratively out of order under BCO 43-1 and because the requested relief was unavailable. A separate opinion concurred in the result but dissented from part of the reasoning and urged clarification of appellate review after an acquittal.

artifacts.title: Systematic overhaul of BCO judicial process chapters 31, 32, and 35

matches.evidence: Overture proposing broad changes to BCO 31, 32, and 35 governing judicial process was found in grave conflict with multiple BCO provisions but adopted 8-0-0.

artifacts.title: Requiring church officers to testify in disciplinary proceedings

matches.evidence: An overture to compel church officer testimony was possibly in conflict with BCO 35-3 and 35-4 regarding the two-witness requirement and exclusion of witnesses during others' testimony.
